headline: North Korea floods open-source package registries with credential-stealing malware even as Cisco's ClamAV races to patch scanner flaws two decades old.

emerging_trends.text: State-backed crews keep turning open-source registries into malware channels, with North Korea's PolinRider seeding npm, Packagist, and Go with credential-stealing code that maintainers must now hunt through their dependency trees.
emerging_trends.topic_title: North Korea Floods Registries With 108 Malicious Packages

emerging_trends.text: The rush to bolt AI onto shipping software compounds faster than teams can patch it, as freshly added large language model features rate high-risk more often than any other vulnerability class.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Bolted-On AI Features Rate High-Risk and Patch Slow

emerging_trends.text: Vendors market privacy features as shields, and those shields keep springing leaks, as Apple's Hide My Email now exposes the real addresses it promises to mask.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Apple's Hide My Email Leaks the Real Address

topics.title: ClamAV Patches Seven Flaws Two Decades Old
topics.latest_developments: Cisco's Talos group shipped ClamAV 1.5.3 and 1.4.5 on July 5, fixing seven security flaws—most sitting in the code that unpacks and parses executable formats—some dating back two decades.
topics.summary: ClamAV, the open-source scanning engine that runs inside mail gateways, file-upload checks, and endpoint tooling at organizations of every size, released the two patch versions with extra hardening. Administrators should upgrade both branches now.

sources.title: New ClamAV security patch closes seven scanner bugs dating back two decades

topics.title: Bolted-On AI Features Rate High-Risk and Patch Slow
topics.latest_developments: Help Net Security's July 5 week-in-review flagged a pattern: companies bolt AI and large language model features onto products, and the resulting vulnerabilities rate high risk far more often than any other class and get fixed slower.
topics.summary: The finding marks a mounting security debt as vendors rush generative-AI features into shipping software. Security teams should treat new AI features as elevated-risk surfaces and press vendors on remediation timelines.

sources.title: Week in review: SimpleHelp vulnerability exploited, Oracle EBS Payments flaw under attack

topics.title: Flipper Zero Firmware Shifts to Community Hands
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer reported July 5 that Flipper Devices will keep developing the Flipper Zero firmware with a smaller internal team and heavier reliance on community contributions.
topics.summary: The Flipper Zero, a pocket multi-tool that penetration testers and hobbyists use to probe RFID, sub-GHz radio, and other protocols, moves to a leaner maintenance model. Users should expect a slower, community-driven release cadence.

sources.title: Flipper Zero firmware development continues with community help

topics.title: North Korea Floods Registries With 108 Malicious Packages
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News reported July 4 that North Korea's Contagious Interview crew published 108 malicious packages and browser extensions across npm, Packagist, Go, and the Chrome Web Store in a campaign researchers call PolinRider.
topics.summary: The Contagious Interview operation compromises maintainer accounts and seeds developer registries with credential-stealing code, and the campaign stays active, so new packages keep appearing. Developers should audit dependencies and lock trusted versions.

sources.title: North Korean Hackers Publish 108 Malicious Packages and Extensions in PolinRider Campaign

topics.title: Apple's Hide My Email Leaks the Real Address
topics.latest_developments: Wired reported July 4 that Apple's Hide My Email—the iCloud+ feature that mints random relay addresses to mask a user's true address—fails to keep that real address hidden.
topics.summary: Hide My Email underpins Apple's privacy pitch across Sign in with Apple and iCloud+, so any leak exposes the very addresses users pay to conceal. Anyone relying on the relays for anonymity should assume their real address can surface.

sources.title: Security Roundup: Apple's Hide My Email Service Fails to Hide Your Email

business_politics.title: NATO Summit Opens Amid Transatlantic Rupture
business_politics.latest_developments: NATO's leaders convened in Ankara on July 5, where chief Mark Rutte said arms makers are straining to keep pace with member spending, as a Wall Street Journal account detailed how President Trump's tariffs and Greenland threats pushed Europe's leaders toward an open break with Washington.
business_politics.summary: The alliance's heads of state met in Ankara to weigh whether pledged spending increases can produce actual munitions, with a signaled U.S. troop drawdown from Europe stoking fears that Washington's retreat emboldens Russia's Vladimir Putin.

sources.title: NATO Is Fixing Its Cash Flow Problem. Now It Needs to Turn Money Into Munitions.
'There Is No Going Back': The Inside Story of Europe's Rupture With America
Nato leaders gather for crucial meeting in Ankara

business_politics.title: Ukrainian Drones Trigger Russia's Worst Fuel Crisis in Decades
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported July 5 that Kyiv has ramped drone strikes on Russian refineries and energy sites to an unprecedented rate, tipping Russia into its worst fuel crisis in decades.
business_politics.summary: Ukraine's intensified drone campaign against Russian oil refineries and fuel depots has driven gasoline and diesel shortages across Russia, squeezing a war-strained economy and one of the world's largest energy exporters.

sources.title: Ukraine striking Russian energy infrastructure at unprecedented rate

around_town.title: Slippery Rock Declares Disaster Emergency
around_town.latest_developments: Slippery Rock Borough Mayor Jondavid Longo signed a disaster-emergency declaration Sunday, July 5, after flash flooding left numerous streets impassable, ordering all residents to stay home.
around_town.summary: Intense Sunday-afternoon rain triggered dangerous flash flooding in Slippery Rock Borough in Butler County, prompting Mayor Jondavid Longo to declare a disaster emergency and first responders to close impassable streets.

sources.title: Slippery Rock Borough declares disaster emergency after intense rainfall
Slippery Rock mayor signs declaration of disaster emergency as borough deals with storms, flooding

around_town.title: Storms Break Rainfall Record as Heat Wave Ends
around_town.latest_developments: Storms dumped 1.97 inches of rain at Pittsburgh International Airport through 7 p.m. Sunday, July 5, breaking the daily record of 1.89 inches set in 2005, as flood warnings covered much of Allegheny County.
around_town.summary: A third straight day of heavy thunderstorms brought localized flash flooding across western Pennsylvania on July 5, with the National Weather Service placing much of the region under flood watches and warnings as cooler, humid air replaced the multi-day heat wave.

sources.title: Pittsburgh's hot weather turns into cool, humid and rainy conditions this week
Flood warnings in effect for much of Allegheny County, northern Westmoreland

around_teams.title: Valdez Emerges as Pirates' Brightest Bat
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's July 4 'Off The Bat' feature charted how young hitter Esmerlyn Valdez has 'arrived' and become 'a dude' for the Pirates, days after columnist Noah Hiles argued he can become what the club once hoped Marcell Ozuna would be.
around_teams.summary: Esmerlyn Valdez, the Pirates' young designated hitter, has become the team's most productive bat during a grim stretch, and Post-Gazette writers now frame him as a genuine middle-of-the-order threat for a lineup starved of offense.

sources.title: Off The Bat: How Esmerlyn Valdez has arrived — and become 'a dude' — for the Pirates
Noah Hiles: Esmerlyn Valdez can be everything the Pirates hoped Marcell Ozuna would be

team_usa.title: Belgium Fumes as FIFA Clears Balogun
team_usa.latest_developments: Belgium reacted with fury to Balogun's reinstatement, coach Rudi Garcia calling it an 'April Fool' joke, while U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino said his team was 'punished enough' and the Guardian reported Trump made three calls to secure the reversal.
team_usa.summary: FIFA's disciplinary committee suspended U.S. striker Folarin Balogun's red-card ban on July 5, freeing him to face Belgium in Seattle on July 6 after President Trump lobbied FIFA president Gianni Infantino, a reversal Belgium's federation called astonishing.

sources.title: Belgium furious at Balogun U-turn: It's April Fool
FIFA suspends Balogun red card, can face Belgium
Trump lobbied Fifa to lift Folarin Balogun suspension for World Cup game v Belgium

team_usa.title: U.S. Teen Taylor Stuns Prefontaine 200
team_usa.latest_developments: American teenager Tate Taylor won the 200 meters at the Prefontaine Classic on July 5, beating a field that included Olympic 200 champion Letsile Tebogo of Botswana.
team_usa.summary: Tate Taylor, a U.S. teenage sprinter, upset the 200-meter field at the Prefontaine Classic in Eugene, Oregon, outrunning Olympic gold medalist Letsile Tebogo in a breakout result.

sources.title: U.S. teen Taylor stuns Prefontaine field to win 200

reading.title: The AI Industry Is Losing
reading.summary: Zitron argues the AI industry is fundamentally losing money and momentum, its enormous build-out failing to yield the profits or products that would justify the spending.

reading.title: Beware of Productivity Paradoxes
reading.summary: Newport warns that technologies seemingly destined to boost output, from the personal computer to today's AI tools, often fail to deliver the productivity gains their promise implies.
